experiment: inject a reference character's captured latent into a DIFFERENT scene's denoise entering step k (scene text still steers the finish); measure latent-cosine similarity of the output to the reference vs to the scene baseline
ref_prompt: a portrait of a woman with distinctive curly red hair and green eyes, plain grey background
reading: Reference-latent injection retention is monotone AND SHARP in k, with the SAME commitment crossover (~k4) as the random-delta perturbation experiment: a random scene is ~orthogonal to the reference (inherent sim 0.013); injecting the reference entering step k drives output-to-reference similarity from 0.29 (k1, scene overwrites it) to 0.98 (k4) to 0.999 (k7, output == reference). Full latent replacement is nearly BINARY around the commitment step -- inject before k4 and the scene wins, after and the reference locks and the scene is ignored. sim_to_scene falls in lockstep (0.10 -> 0.014). The two scenes give near-identical curves -> the pin behavior is scene-independent (generalizes across images). The identity-in-a-new-scene window is the narrow pre-commitment band (k~2-4); a blend there is how you mix character and context.
